new_removed_recheck.concept: health awareness content with credible background
new_removed_recheck.reason: Tested 'health awareness content with credible background' as a transformation of '30% influencer review'. Narrowed: 'Health awareness content with credible background' is not a specific way of being influencer review (different content categories — product/service review vs health awareness education). Reframed: while both involve influencers, the organizing frame shifts from 'review of product' to 'health awareness content with credible endorsement', which is more than a frame shift on the same territory — the content category itself changes. Elaborated: '30% influencer review' does not contain a seed that yields health awareness content when detail is added; adding 'health awareness' introduces a new content domain. Expanded: cannot identify a pre-antecedent that broadens into health awareness. All four fail as standalone transformations of the influencer review concept. However, treating 'health awareness content' as a New event alongside a matched 'influencer review → influencers with credible background' split would double-count the POST span. The defensible reading is that the POST concept bundles two ideas (influencer involvement + health awareness content type) that partially map back to PRE; the influencer element finds a successor but the health awareness content type does not. Per the mandatory re-check, the influencer portion converts into the matched pair already coded, and the health-awareness content category portion is absorbed into that event's evidence rather than emitted as a separate New. The single matched pair '30% influencer review → Health awareness content with influencers that have credible background' captures the transformation, with the thematic-content shift noted in the rationale.

structural_development.rationale: The PRE is a terse two-clause allocation (70/30 split between two content types). The POST introduces a new thematic content category ('health awareness content'), adds a credibility qualifier for influencers ('that have credible background'), and retains 'product review' in bare form. Net change: one new content type introduced, one qualifier introduced, the original ratio framing is dropped, and existing categories are partly re-described. This is more than stylistic — a new content pillar and a credibility criterion were added — but it does not reach the level of multiple new sentences or explanatory passages; it is a contained expansion at the clause level.

semantic_events.post_evidence: Health awareness content with influencers that have credible background
semantic_events.rationale: Same semantic neighborhood (influencer-driven content), but the organizing frame shifts from a review-of-product allocation to a thematic health-awareness content model with a credibility-qualifier on the influencer. PRE frame: ratio-allocated influencer review. POST frame: thematically-organized health awareness content delivered by credentialed influencers. Not subsumption (health awareness content is not a specific way of being influencer review). Not elaboration (the content category itself changes, not just added detail to review).

The 70% allocation qualifier and the ratio framing are absent from the POST. The nearest POST counterpart is 'product review', which retains the content category but not the 70% allocation. Tested Narrowed: 'bare product review' is not a specific way of being '70% product review' — the allocation is dropped, not specified. Tested Reframed: product review content category persists, but no frame shift occurs — the change is a drop of the allocation number, which is closer to a removed qualifier than a reframing. Tested Elaborated: no detail added to the allocation. Tested Expanded: no broadening of the allocation concept. The 70% ratio figure has no semantic successor in POST and is not a generic filler that gets subsumed; it is a quantitative allocation that was dropped. The content category itself persists via the matched pair with bare 'product review', so the category is accounted for; only the 70% allocation is removed.

uncertainty.coder_notes: The 70% allocation qualifier in PRE ('70% product review') is treated as Removed because no POST element carries the ratio figure; the bare content category 'product review' is retained via the matched pair. The 30% influencer review tracks to the influencer portion of the POST concept, but the health-awareness content type is new. Because splitting the POST span across two events would risk double-counting, the influencer-to-credible-influencer transition is captured as a single Reframed event with the full POST span as evidence and the thematic shift noted in the rationale. The health-awareness content type is not emitted as a separate New event because it is bundled inside the matched pair's post_evidence; this is a judgment call documented for auditability.
